entities.name: Laodice IV
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Laodice IV was a Greek princess and head priestess of the Seleucid Empire, serving under her brother Antiochus III. She was appointed as the chief priestess of the state cult dedicated to her mother Laodice III in Media.


Laodice IV married three kings of the Seleucid Empire, all of whom were her brothers.


She played a significant role in the religious and political landscape of the Seleucid Empire during the 2nd century BCE.


Laodice IV's legacy is marked by her influence on the development of the Seleucid state and its relationships with neighboring regions.


The Greek historian Polybius is said to have praised Laodice IV for her wisdom and piety.


Despite her significance, Laodice IV's life remains somewhat overshadowed by that of her more famous contemporaries.


The Hellenistic period's complex web of royal marriages and alliances, however, underscores the importance of Laodice IV's position and influence.
